claims.text: An active-learning ML interatomic potential combined with thermodynamic integration and selective ab initio corrections can reproduce fusion free energies within 5% of full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The proposed workflow can reduce computational cost by at least one order of magnitude relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The ML potential will be trained on strategically selected ab initio MD snapshots from regions critical to the phase transition.
The trained ML potential will be used in thermodynamic integration with periodic ab initio corrections.
The method is intended to treat both solid and liquid phases near melting.
Vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling are fully captured in the targeted states.
Selectively corrected ML evaluations accurately reproduce free-energy surfaces containing vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration contributions.
Active learning preferentially refines the potential in the free-energy-landscape regions where phase-transition physics is most complex.
The ML potential enables rapid interpolation of ab initio energies and forces.
Periodic ab initio corrections preserve the fidelity of entropy contributions.
The hybrid workflow preserves the physical details required for fusion calculations while reducing computational workload.
The workflow will scale better than TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Explicit ab initio MD free-energy evaluations are accurate but computationally expensive.
TOR-TILD scales poorly for complex multicomponent systems.
Interatomic-potential methods are applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys and can agree quantitatively with selected first-principles and experimental properties.
The proposed workflow is applicable across elemental systems, binary alloys, and complex high-entropy alloys.
The target temperature range is within approximately 10–20% above or below the experimental melting temperature.
Extreme configurational disorder that is inadequately represented in the initial ab initio snapshots may limit the method.
The benchmark will compare solid–liquid phase free-energy differences, melting temperatures, and latent heats against full ab initio MD results.
Deviations greater than 5% in phase free energies or derived melting properties across multiple benchmark systems will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and mediator fields state that electron–vibration coupling, anharmonicity, and related entropy effects are fully or accurately captured, whereas the uncertainty field says the ML potential's ability to capture these effects remains unestablished. This should be framed as a target rather than an achieved property.
